Connect Solar Project Spending with Billing and Cash Records

Thematic Area: Solar Project Finance Operations & Cost Control

How might we connect project purchases, spending approvals and customer balances to improve visibility of solar project costs and cash requirements?

Background

An Indonesian solar EPC business has identified project management as a priority. The opportunity is to connect project spending, customer billing and cash records within that delivery workflow.

The objective is to give project and finance teams a usable view of commitments, actual spending, billing and outstanding payments. Relevant startups offer invoice matching, project budgets, spending approvals and receivables management.

The solution should connect accounting records with project codes, milestones and approval rules, supporting consistent management views of cost and cash requirements.

Significance of Problem

Without an effective solution, the challenges include:

  • Limited cost visibility: Incomplete links between purchases and budgets make project spending harder to track.
  • Difficult cash planning: Fragmented records make customer balances and upcoming commitments harder to compare.
  • More reconciliation work: Invoice discrepancies and inconsistent records increase manual financial investigation.

Existing Efforts

  • Opportunity focus: Bring cost control, billing and collections information together to support solar project management.
  • Available partner capability: A finance-automation provider compares supplier invoices with purchase orders and goods receipts. It also offers spending approvals, budget controls, customer-balance tracking, reconciliation and collection reminders.
  • Collaboration focus: Connect a selected project’s purchases and customer balances with the accounting system. Represent commitments, changes, milestones and actual costs consistently. Measure record accuracy and exception resolution, and build management views that follow Indonesian finance and accounting requirements.

Potential Market Size

  • Solar capital expenditure: Global investment in solar power projects is estimated at US$365 billion in 2026, showing the scale of spending associated with solar delivery.

Eligibility / Qualification

  • Technology readiness: Minimum technology readiness level 3 (TRL3).
  • NUS linkage: NUS student or graduate founder, or incubation through an NUS programme such as BLOCK71.
  • Local and overseas startups: Open to Indonesian and overseas startups.
  • Commitment: Complete the selection process and travel to Indonesia if selected.
